fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Mason Who Walked Out and Went Deeper", "body": "Joe Rupe opens by explaining why he left Freemasonry around 2013 and moved into Golden Dawn ceremonial work instead. He insists he did not leave because the craft is corrupt in principle but because it is beautiful and badly corrupted where he lives. Chance Garton pushes on the scapegoating of Masonry, and Gabe adds that during the lockdowns people rediscovered private membership associations for exactly the sanctuary and mutual protection lodges once provided. Joe describes clandestine lodges in Europe calling themselves vampires, and argues the fundamentals still matter more than the wreckage history made of them."}, {"title": "Bored at Tech Support, Then Out of His Body", "body": "Joe traces his entire path back to a corporate tech support job where boredom led him to Robert Monroe's audiobook Journeys Out of the Body. He tried projecting on lunch breaks until he had what he calls an etheric projection, distinct from lucid dreaming or astral travel. Chance shares his own single clear projection during a multiday liquid cleanse, floating into the ceiling fan and hallway before losing the thread. Joe lays out the layers involved, the etheric double, the silver cord he has never actually seen, and why no objective proof of any of it exists."}, {"title": "The Four Trees Hidden Inside the Tarot", "body": "The longest teaching stretch is Joe explaining the four Kabbalistic worlds, Atziluth, Briah, Yetzirah and Assiah, and how a whole tree of life sits inside each one. Numbered cards map to sephiroth, court cards map to parts of the soul, and Crowley placed the knight in Chokmah and the princes in Tiphareth where Christ energy balances everything. Arthur Edward Waite deliberately hid the Kabbalistic keys because the Golden Dawn told him to, while Crowley blew the lid off with colors, god forms and tantric alchemy. Chance calls this genuinely new to him."}, {"title": "Balance Over Renunciation", "body": "Both hosts reject the idea that material gain is the opposite of spirituality. Chance calls that split priest jive, the same logic that codes matter, darkness and the feminine as evil. Joe compares the soul to a battery whose highest energy sits at the balance point, and points listeners to the Devil and Lovers cards, which share the same sephirothic structure but differ in whether the chain is worn or removed. Chance connects this to his biofield tuning sessions, where men his age routinely have the entire anger spectrum nullified out of their fields, and argues a fully realized morality knows its own capacity for harm."}, {"title": "Contact Experience as Repressed Human Power", "body": "Chance frames the paranormal through Jungian depth psychology, arguing that if the psyche has layers then so does the cosmos, and that encounters with aliens, angels, demons or fairies may be latent human capacities bursting through the seams of repression. People permit themselves levitation only when gray aliens are doing it. Joe agrees, adding that many ghosts are living people wandering in their etheric bodies, and that the astral world holds every archetype, blueprint and prayer. Gabe decodes Obi-Wan Kenobi as the Enneagram observer, and Joe reads Blue Oyster Cult's Don't Fear the Reaper as Saturn's cycles."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight we welcome Joe Rupe to Vibe Rant. In addition to hosting his long-running radio style podcast, Lighting the Void, Joe's also the man behind The Fringe FM, a network of like-minded esoteric explorers. With years of experience examining the occult and expanded consciousness research, Joe brings a wide array of knowledge that will absolutely make for a fascinating mind meld.
